title: Given a Scenario, Use the Appropriate Microsoft Command-Line Tools

sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: Windows command-line tools navigate folders, test networking, manage disks and files, gather information, and manage the operating system.
The main mental model is: navigate → network → disk → files → information → OS management.
sections.callout: Choose a command for the task it performs, not simply because its name looks familiar.

sections.title: Maestro Focus
paragraphs: When a Windows scenario describes a task, can you choose the correct command and basic syntax pattern?

entries.title: cd
paragraphs: cd means change directory and moves the command prompt to another folder. Example: cd Documents.
entries.recognitionCue: Move from the current folder into another → cd.

entries.title: dir
paragraphs: dir lists a directory's files, folders, dates, and sizes.
entries.recognitionCue: See what is in the current folder → dir.

entries.title: ipconfig
paragraphs: ipconfig displays Windows TCP/IP configuration; ipconfig /all adds detailed adapter, DNS, and DHCP information.
entries.recognitionCue: Verify the local address, mask, gateway, DNS, or DHCP data → ipconfig.

entries.title: ping
paragraphs: ping uses ICMP echo messages to test basic IP reachability when ICMP is allowed.
entries.recognitionCue: Can this computer reach the destination? → ping.

entries.title: netstat
paragraphs: netstat displays active connections, listening ports, local and remote addresses, and protocol statistics.
entries.recognitionCue: Inspect current TCP/UDP connections and ports → netstat.

entries.title: nslookup
paragraphs: nslookup queries DNS to resolve names or addresses and test name resolution.
entries.recognitionCue: IP connectivity works but a hostname does not resolve → nslookup.

entries.title: net use
paragraphs: net use connects to and manages network resources such as shared folders and mapped drives. Example: net use Z: \\server\share.
entries.recognitionCue: Map a share to a drive letter → net use.

entries.title: tracert
paragraphs: tracert displays the intermediate network hops to a destination.
entries.recognitionCue: Determine which routers traffic crosses → tracert.

entries.title: pathping
paragraphs: pathping combines route tracing with latency and packet-loss measurements and takes longer while it gathers statistics.
entries.recognitionCue: Find the hop where delay or packet loss may occur → pathping.

sections.title: Disk Management

entries.title: chkdsk
paragraphs: chkdsk checks a volume and filesystem for errors and can repair supported problems with appropriate options.
entries.recognitionCue: Suspected filesystem corruption → chkdsk.

entries.title: format
paragraphs: format creates a filesystem on a volume. It can destroy existing target data, so verify the drive before use.
entries.recognitionCue: Prepare a volume with a filesystem → format.

entries.title: diskpart
paragraphs: diskpart is a powerful interactive tool for disks, partitions, and volumes. Commands such as list disk and list volume inspect storage; other operations can be destructive.
entries.recognitionCue: Manage disk or partition structure from the command line → diskpart.

sections.callout: Check filesystem → chkdsk. Create filesystem → format. Manage storage structure → diskpart.

entries.title: md
paragraphs: md, also available as mkdir, creates a directory.
entries.recognitionCue: Create a folder → md.

entries.title: rmdir
paragraphs: rmdir removes a directory when its contents and selected options allow removal.
entries.recognitionCue: Remove a directory → rmdir.

entries.title: robocopy
paragraphs: Robust File Copy reliably copies files and directory trees for large, repeated, recursive, or network transfer jobs.
entries.recognitionCue: Reliably copy a large folder tree → robocopy.

entries.title: hostname
paragraphs: hostname displays the computer's host name.
entries.recognitionCue: Which computer is this? → hostname.

entries.title: net user
paragraphs: net user displays or manages local Windows user accounts.
entries.recognitionCue: View or manage local users at the command line → net user.

entries.title: winver
paragraphs: winver displays the Windows version and build interface.
entries.recognitionCue: Quickly identify the Windows release or build → winver.

entries.title: whoami
paragraphs: whoami displays the current user or security context.
entries.recognitionCue: Confirm which account the shell is running as → whoami.

entries.title: [command name] /?
paragraphs: Appending /? to many Windows commands displays their built-in syntax and options. Example: ipconfig /?.
entries.recognitionCue: Need command options without an external reference → [command] /?.

sections.title: OS Management

entries.title: gpupdate
paragraphs: gpupdate refreshes and reapplies Group Policy settings.
entries.recognitionCue: A changed policy should be refreshed now → gpupdate.

entries.title: gpresult
paragraphs: gpresult reports which Group Policy settings have been applied to a computer or user.
entries.recognitionCue: Verify which policies actually applied → gpresult.

entries.title: sfc
paragraphs: System File Checker verifies protected Windows system files and can repair damaged copies. The familiar form is sfc /scannow.
entries.recognitionCue: Protected Windows files may be corrupt → sfc /scannow.

sections.callout: Refresh policy → gpupdate. Report applied policy → gpresult.

entries.title: ping vs. tracert vs. pathping
paragraphs: ping tests reachability; tracert lists hops; pathping adds loss and latency statistics per hop.

entries.title: ipconfig vs. nslookup
paragraphs: ipconfig shows local configuration; nslookup tests DNS.

entries.title: chkdsk vs. format vs. diskpart
paragraphs: chkdsk checks a filesystem; format creates one; diskpart manages disk and partition structure.

entries.title: hostname vs. whoami
paragraphs: hostname identifies the computer; whoami identifies the current user context.

entries.title: gpupdate vs. gpresult
paragraphs: gpupdate refreshes policy; gpresult reports applied policy.
